result.title: RE: INVESTMENT CONSULTING SERVICES
key_items: City of Grand Rapids General Retirement System; City of Grand Rapids Police and Fire Retirement System
City of Grand Rapids General Retirement System
City of Grand Rapids Police and Fire Retirement System
result.summary: A July 27, 2023 RFP seeks investment consulting proposals for the City of Grand Rapids General Retirement System and Police and Fire Retirement System, due by 4:00 p.m. Thursday, August 31, 2023. Their Boards are reviewing consulting services and invite proposals for general (non-discretionary) services, discretionary OCIO services, or both. Plan information is available at grpensions.org. As of June 30, 2023, the General System had approximately $437 million in assets, allocated to fixed income (24%), U.S. equity (17%), global equity (10%), non-U.S. equity and ADRs (8% each), private equity, TIPS, REITs, commodities, mid-stream energy, and private credit (5% each). The Police and Fire System had approximately $479 million, allocated to fixed income (23%), U.S. equity (19%), global equity (10%), ADRs (9%), non-U.S. equity (8%), private equity (7%), TIPS, REITs, commodities, and mid-stream energy (5% each), and private credit (4%). Northern Trust is the asset custodian.

result.title: A. SCOPE OF SERVICES
result.summary: The investment consultant provides objective third-party advice to help the Board make informed decisions about Plan assets. Services include developing and periodically reviewing investment policies, objectives and guidelines; conducting asset-allocation studies; assisting with investment-manager searches and due diligence; establishing and reviewing manager performance standards; attending Board meetings as requested; and providing general consulting, including custodial searches. The consultant monitors manager performance and Act 314 compliance and submits written quarterly reports on both. It also advises on manager diversification and, upon request, provides holdings and transaction information for securities-litigation claims. Fully discretionary investment management is optional if the Boards choose an OCIO agreement.

result.title: B. MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS
result.summary:
B. MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS
1. The Investment Consultant must have a minimum of five (5) years of experience in providing institutional investor consulting services.
2. The Investment Consultant must provide services to at least one (1) public employee retirement system with at least $250 million in assets.
3. The Investment Consultant must be a registered investment advisor under the Investment Advisors Act of 1940.
4. The Investment Consultant shall acknowledge its responsibilities as an investment fiduciary under Public Act 314 of 1965, as amended.
5. If you are affiliating or partnering with a national firm, or are a local office of a national firm, the minimum qualification requirements herein must be satisfied by the individual or entity submitting this proposal.
6. The Investment Consultant must attend regular meetings, as well as special meetings upon request by the Board, at no additional cost to the Plan. The Board currently meets nine times per year.

result.title: C. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS
key_items: II. REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL – Please label each response with the corresponding question’s section and number.
result.summary: Submissions must include a title page with the RFP subject, organization name and address, telephone number, contact person, and date; a table of contents with sections and page numbers; and answers to Section II questions in order, labeled with each question’s section and number. Submit one copy in a sealed envelope marked “RFP: Investment Consulting Services” to the City of Grand Rapids Retirement Systems, 233 East Fulton, Suite 216, Grand Rapids, MI 49503, and email an electronic copy to Peggy Korzen (info@grpensions.org) and Thomas Michaud (tmichaud@vmtlaw.com). Submit questions in writing to Peggy Korzen at least seven days before the proposal deadline; later questions will not be considered. Email intent to respond by 4:00 p.m. August 15, 2023. Proposals must arrive at the stated address by 4:00 p.m. August 31, 2023; late submissions will not be accepted.

result.title: A. FIRM INFORMATION
result.summary: The request seeks firm contact and authorized-presenter details; understanding of the work; ownership and affiliate relationships, related retirement services, conflict safeguards, and use of proprietary investments in searches; employee count and three-year departures; nearest office to Grand Rapids; assigned consultants’ biographies, locations, meeting attendance, and experience; public pension clients, at least three references, and national/Michigan assets-under-advisement by size tier (as of June 30, 2023, or another stated date); and clients lost in the past three years, including discretionary status. It also asks about performance-measurement database size, composition, sources, and comparison indices; qualifications; business relationships with investment managers or trust-fund service providers; a complete latest SEC Form ADV; commission recapture and its service implications; MAPERS membership; and whether the firm will conduct an on-site due-diligence visit, with details and a sample agenda.

result.title: B. INVESTMENT POLICY/ASSET ALLOCATION GUIDELINES
result.summary:
B. INVESTMENT POLICY/ASSET ALLOCATION GUIDELINES
1. Provide an outline of the steps you would follow when developing a statement of Investment Policy and Objectives. Does your investment policy and asset allocation analysis fully integrate liabilities with assets? How do you interface with the Plan’s actuary?
2. How many meetings would be required with the Board throughout this process? Who would attend from your firm?
3. Provide an outline of the issues and items that would be covered in a typical investment policy statement.
4. What is your approach to development of asset allocation guidelines? Please describe this process in detail, including application of major variables (e.g. - risk tolerance, emerging liabilities, etc.).
5. What asset classes are included in your work?
6. What geographic areas of the world do you consider appropriate for Plan asset investments?
7. Does your approach include passive strategies such as indexing? If so, please describe.
6

result.title: C. INVESTMENT MANAGER SELECTION
result.summary:
C. INVESTMENT MANAGER SELECTION
1. What is the procedure and criteria you follow in the selection of investment managers? What is the typical timeframe from start to finish?
2. How many firms do you track for manager search purposes?
3. Do the individual consultants assigned to our account interface with prospective managers? If so, please explain your due diligence process.
4. What resources do you utilize for manager screening? Which are purchased and which are proprietary?
5. Explain how you monitor and measure the level of success of existing managers. Please be specific.
6. What criteria is used to recommend termination of a manager?
7. Do you believe that when a manager is not performing that the consultant who presented this manager also be held accountable? If so, how? If not, why?
8. Do you have any arrangements with broker-dealers under which you or a related company will benefit if money managers place trades for their clients with such broker-dealers?

result.title: D. PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
result.summary: The section requests details on the firm’s performance evaluation system and its philosophy, whether proprietary or sourced; report delivery timelines and recommended review frequency; sample reports and customization options; and any firm-created indices. It asks the firm to describe its preferred role with the Plan and other client services. It requests annualized 1-, 3-, 5-, and 10-year results through December 31, 2022, for three nondiscretionary public employee plan clients, preferably Michigan plans, including policy-index comparisons, and optionally asset-class results, benchmarks, peer rankings, client asset size, allocation, location, and performance commentary. It also asks whether the firm completes securities-action proof-of-claim documents and charges for doing so, how the Board should evaluate its consultant, and how the firm monitors brokerage services for best cost and execution.

result.title: E. CUSTODIAL SERVICES
result.summary:
E. CUSTODIAL SERVICES
1. Does your firm provide custodial services? If so, please provide details.

result.title: F. DISCRETIONARY INVESTMENT MANAGEMENT SERVICES
result.summary: The questionnaire asks about the firm’s discretionary/OCIO services, history and revenue, assets under discretionary management versus non-discretionary advisement, investment philosophy and processes, and how it incorporates plan goals, risk preferences, liabilities, and actuarial input. It covers active versus passive management, cash levels, current positioning and its duration, model versus customized portfolios, experience and intended roles of alternative assets, public–private market trade-offs in current conditions, and target allocations for underfunded and overfunded plans. It also requests three distinctive manager-research capabilities for identifying alpha, asset-transition practices including treatment of illiquid holdings, and trading policies for best execution, equitable treatment, exceptions, and trade allocation. Finally, it asks for views on discretionary versus non-discretionary management, the fiduciary bond carrier, disaster recovery and ethics policies, and procedures for complying with client investment policy statements and maintaining asset-management quality control.

result.title: G. FEES
result.summary: The questionnaire asks for detailed fee schedules and discretionary-management costs, hard-dollar alternatives, travel and other expenses, quarterly billing in arrears, and soft-dollar rates, conversion, and reporting. It asks about client-directed brokerage, SEC/NASD complaints, litigation, lawsuits, regulatory investigations, adviser registration and required disclosures. It also covers relationships with and payments from recommended money managers, related-company interests, conflict-of-interest safeguards, use and monitoring of brokerage commissions to pay fees, best-execution protections, and broker-dealer arrangements that may benefit the firm. Respondents must address written and recommendation-related fiduciary status, the share of institutional clients using providers that pay the firm fees, and the types and dollar coverage of client-protective insurance and indemnification.

result.title: OTHER REQUIREMENTS
result.summary: The RFP states that inviting proposals does not pre-qualify responders, and the Board will not reimburse proposal-preparation costs. Submitting a proposal confirms the responder has read and understands the RFP and its work requirements, and indicates agreement to its provisions unless stated otherwise. Responders must provide additional reasonably requested information; the Board may investigate their qualifications. Consultants must not contact individual trustees or other Plan members outside designated contacts, as doing so may disqualify them. The Board may reject any or all proposals, select the proposal it considers most favorable, waive minor procedural irregularities, or seek new proposals. Proposals remain binding for 90 calendar days after the submission deadline; late proposals will not be considered, and submissions must include all required information. The Plan thanks respondents for their time and effort.
